svg.text: V2 HLD — THE SAME LOOP AS V1, AS A SMALL SERVICE · A TURN IS A JOB · THE ANSWER STREAMS BACK
User
asks a question
job id back · then the stream
Orchestrator service
one service, two layers: the HTTP face and the loop
API layer — HTTP
POST /runs → job id at once
GET /turns/{id} · steps, answer
GET /turns/{id}/events · SSE
agents and tools: metadata files
forwards the run's stream
to the client, by job id
Orchestrator — the loop
build the context (the question + the rows so far)
ask the model → run what it names → write the row → ask again
until the model says done · then the answer, relayed and streamed
every row in the store before the next step is taken
several tools in one reply run together · a clock on every call
an agent can be a tool: a child loop inside the call
a repeated call is a reference · caps on passes, calls, depth
the loop's two seams are the boxes on the right
LLM proxy — the model interface
takes the context · answers with a tool call and its input, or done
in this POC: a rule-based stub, keywords on the question,
then the ids the results name
in production: a real model on a GPU, behind the same interface
shared by every customer · the scaling and performance pages
①
②
Tool caller + Tool registry
tools from tools/*.json · the type picks the adapter
lookup · sleep · fail · agent, under the agent's tool list and clock
in this POC: lookups over data in the tool file
in production: REST and MCP calls as the user, same adapter seam
③
④
Run store — SQLite
conversation → turn (job id) → span rows
the tenant database at scale
each step · before the next
the turn row
the run's stream: each step, each answer token
SSE: steps and answer tokens

① the context · ② a tool to call with its input, or done · ③ the call · ④ the result, written as a row, then ① again. v1 drew exactly this loop; v2 keeps it and puts the service, the store and the stream around it.
Blue = the loop and its model seam, this document's subject · orange = what sits behind the model interface in production · dashed = the stream back to the client.
